183.solution: Let $A$, $M$, and $L$ denote clients buying annuities, mutual funds, and life insurance. 188.solution: Let $A$ denote wanting life policy P, $B$ wanting life policy Q, and $C$ wanting the health policy. The disjoint Venn regions have probabilities $a$ in $A$ only, $b$ in $A\cap C$, $0.18$ in $C$ only, $c$ in $B\cap C$, and $d$ in $B$ only; $A\cap B=\varnothing$. Conditions (ii) and (iii) give $a+b=2(c+d)$ and $b+c+0.18=0.45$, so $b+c=0.27$. Condition (v) gives $P((A\cup B)\cap C)=P(A\cup B)P(C)$, or $b+c=(a+b+c+d)(0.45)$. Therefore $0.27=(a+d+0.27)(0.45)$, so $a+d=0.33$. The desired probability is $a+0.18+d=0.51$.

186.solution: Let $T$ be the event that two red and two blue balls are transferred, and $B$ the event that a blue ball is drawn. Then $P(T\mid B)=P(T\cap B)/P(B)$. The denominator is $$P(B)=\frac{\binom80\binom64}{\binom{14}4}\frac44+\frac{\binom81\binom63}{\binom{14}4}\frac34+\frac{\binom82\binom62}{\binom{14}4}\frac24+\frac{\binom83\binom61}{\binom{14}4}\frac14=\frac{1716}{4004}.$$ Therefore $P(T\mid B)=840/1716\approx0.49$.

727.solution: Let $X$ be the exponential loss with mean $\beta$. The payout is $Y=(X-0.4\beta)_+$. By memorylessness, $E(Y)=P(X>0.4\beta)E(X-0.4\beta\mid X>0.4\beta)=e^{-0.4}\beta$. Thus $1200=e^{-0.4}\beta$, so $\beta=1200e^{0.4}\approx1790$, option B.
